verdicts.value: William Stryker, a military scientist with ties to Logan's past, attacks the school and captures Xavier to use Cerebro to kill every mutant on Earth. The X-Men team up with Magneto to stop him. As they escape a flooding dam, Jean Grey stays behind to hold back the water, and is lost.
verdicts.why: Real status: The Last Stand shows Jean survived the flood at Alkali Lake, so 'dies' is false; 'is lost' matches the status row and spoils nothing.

verdicts.value: ["Logan and Charles: none, the X-Men are gone. Laura: none, escaped from Transigen", "Logan"]
verdicts.why: A stage must be true until the next one: in Logan (2029) the X-Men are dead after Charles's seizure and he and Logan hide in Mexico, so add this stage at Logan (new stage after index 1).

verdicts.value: Jane Foster is infected with the Aether, an ancient weapon wanted by Malekith and his Dark Elves. They attack Asgard and kill Thor's mother, Frigga. Thor frees Loki to help him, and Loki seems to die saving his brother. Thor stops Malekith during the Convergence and turns down the throne, and the Aether, an Infinity Stone, is handed to the Collector for safekeeping. On Asgard's throne, Odin is really Loki in disguise.
verdicts.why: Rule 37: naming which Infinity Stone before the films say so gives it away; The Dark World only calls it an Infinity Stone, and 'Reality Stone' is first said in Infinity War.

verdicts.value: Peter Quill, taken from Earth as a boy the night his mother died, steals an orb that Ronan the Accuser wants for Thanos. He's arrested with Gamora, Thanos's adopted daughter, and bounty hunters Rocket and Groot, and they escape prison with Drax, who lost his family to Ronan. The orb holds an Infinity Stone. When Ronan tries to use it to destroy Xandar, the five hold the stone together and destroy him. Groot sacrifices himself and regrows as a sapling, and the five call themselves the Guardians of the Galaxy.
verdicts.why: Rule 37: the film only calls it an Infinity Stone (Ronan: 'it contains an Infinity Stone'); 'Power Stone' is first said by Thor in Infinity War.

verdicts.value: On TheDailyBugle.net, J. Jonah Jameson calls Spider-Man a fraud and Mysterio a hero, then airs the rest of Mysterio's video. Later, Betty Brant reports lightning storms and sandstorms in New York, and the Bugle blames the Spider-Menace.
verdicts.why: The TikTok has Betty report thunderstorms and sandstorms and guess villains are back, without naming anyone; naming Electro and Sandman also gives away No Way Home, which comes next in this chapter.
Both plot summaries leave out drugs and alcohol, but leaving something out does not show it is false; under the evidence rule an unshown error passes.
Rule 37: Wilson Fisk is on screen as the crime boss, and 'Kingpin' is a name not yet spoken that gives no later reveal away, like Ronin; the group-name rule covers groups only.
